what: A line arrow (chevron head + shaft line) changes shape by state between a down hook (↓), right (→) and up hook (↑) in .42s — rather than simply moving the points, each line bends sideways midway along the path (max 16px, sin curve) and then straightens as it changes, so the chevron and shaft seem to resettle while twisting in opposite directions (cubic in-out curve). For a scroll button that signals the vertical descending stretch, the horizontal flowing stretch, and the end (back to top).

options.shape: Initial Type down · normal · up, default down — change the element’s data-shape or send an fx:shape event (Type name in detail) and it switches to that Type
options.bend: Bend strength multiplier, default 1 — 0 moves straight

use: <button data-fx="arrow-bend-morph" data-shape="down"><svg viewBox="0 0 300 300"><path data-fx-part="head"/><path data-fx-part="body"/></svg> SCROLL</button>

from.where: shared.js .h-scroll SCROLL button — vertical section ↘ · horizontal strip → · closing ↗
